target_customer: Households, small businesses, and robotics developers and researchers
problem: General purpose robots cost tens of thousands of dollars, so homes and small businesses cannot buy them.
business_model: Hardware sales at $1,688 per robot plus a skills marketplace
product_category: Low cost bimanual mobile manipulator robots

founders.name: Antonio Sitong Li
previous_startups: Truely (2,000+ users per YC page), outcome not stated
founders.background_notes: Research fellowships at Laidlaw Scholars, Data Science Institute, Graphics and UI Lab; national patent for a computer vision system per YC page

technical_complexity.rationale: A wheeled dual arm robot with 19 degrees of freedom on commodity compute is a hardware integration job; learning from teleoperation is harder.

defensibility.rationale: Price is the wedge; copyable, though fleet data could compound.

market_need_then: Coverage frames strong consumer curiosity for sub $2,000 robots; company reports over $440K in sales (company claim) and a sold out first batch per one German outlet.

branding.domain_note: norirobotics.com, exact name plus robotics suffix

identity.visual_style: Product page with friendly 'warming up' copy
identity.voice_and_tone: Short, confident, value led: 'The most capable robot for $1,688'

brand_strength.rationale: Price led launch drew wide press (Interesting Engineering, New Atlas, Forbes per secondary mention, Hacker News launch), which shows the headline helps awareness.

outcome_analysis: Nori Robotics launched a $1,688 wheeled bimanual robot with a viral price headline and wide trade press in summer 2026, plus reported sales and first deliveries. It is early with no exit and no verified funding. Risks are quality and support at that price and that product names changed across sources. Success factors are tentative.
notes: Dealroom lists a $125K seed with YC as investor; single aggregator, unverified, not recorded as a round. Sources conflict on location (NYC vs San Francisco), team size (4 vs 5) and model names (A3, L2, L3). YC page lists only one founder though page text says founders. $440K sales is a company claim. Forbes article seen only secondhand. Update: the 125K seed with Y Combinator rests on a single database (Dealroom, undated; the investor column was blank in a later look). Cross-check searches found no press report of a round.
